- **The repo has no tests and no test config.** No `tests/` directory, no test files, no `pytest.ini`/`pyproject.toml`/`setup.cfg`, no dependency manifest. - **The `tests/test_pricing_cache.py::test_falls_back_to_snapshot` path in the examples is illustrative**, not a real file. If you'd prefer generic placeholders, that's a quick edit.

I verified `python -m pytest` runs in this environment (pytest is already installed) and exits with "no tests ran" — which is what the README tells the reader to expect. If you have an actual test command in mind (a Makefile target, `unittest` discovery, tox), point me at it and I'll replace the section with the real thing.

diff --git a/README.md b/README.md
index 7505656..5dc1aca 100644
--- a/README.md
+++ b/README.md
@@ -1 +1,25 @@
 # fixture repo
+
+## Running the tests
+
+There is no test suite in the repository yet. Tests are expected to live in a
+`tests/` directory alongside the modules they cover, using [pytest][pytest].
+
+Install pytest, then run the suite from the repository root:
+
+```sh
+python -m pip install pytest
+python -m pytest
+```
+
+To run a single file or a single test:
+
+```sh
+python -m pytest tests/test_pricing_cache.py
+python -m pytest tests/test_pricing_cache.py::test_falls_back_to_snapshot
+```
+
+Until the first tests are added, `python -m pytest` exits reporting that no
+tests were collected.
+
+[pytest]: https://docs.pytest.org/
